what: In next/, while the lead of PR 1612 ran the tezgah focus, fold and frame laws 30 times in a row in a cloud container (the plan's T2 proof for slice A), it started pnpm lint beside the loop. The container's memory limit was reached: the kernel killed the test's two headless Chromium processes and lint's tsc. Run 5's tezgah-focus scenario then failed at its first step, 'the grant line as shown grants' (tezgah-focus.visual.test.ts:115), and lint:promise-types failed with EPIPE. Runs 1 to 4 passed.
cause: The lead's slip: two heavy jobs at once in one memory limit. lint runs tsc for lint:promise-types (about 2.4 GB resident here) while each loop run held workerd, two Chromium tabs and vitest. The kernel log names the killed processes (chrome-headless twice, then tsc).
fix: Run 5 is not counted. The 30 in a row are counted from run 6, with no other job beside the loop, and lint runs again after it ends. The PR says so.
test: Code that would have caught it: the loop and pnpm lint taking the same lock that pnpm typecheck takes, so a second heavy job waits instead of sharing the memory limit.
